text:
sasha_customer: Hey team — invoice jumped 2.7k tokens for a single request on Jan 15 (call id: c-abc123). Our local SDK estimator shows ~9.6k tokens; invoice says 12.3k. I can repro locally, sharing payload and quick steps.

rachel_support: Thanks for filing — can you paste the exact request you sent (redact secrets) and the SDK estimator output? Also which SDK version?

sasha_customer: Node SDK v2.5.1. Here's a minimized repro (redacted):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACT' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{\n    "model": "rwd-2b",\n    "messages": [\n      {"role":"system","content":"You are an assistant."},\n      {"role":"user","content":"Process this file and summarize."} \n    ],\n    "tools": [\n      {"name":"file_processor","input":{"filename":"invoice.pdf","contents":"JVBERi0xLjQK...base64..."}}\n  ]\n}'\n```

sasha_customer: Local SDK estimator output: prompt 4,200 tokens, expected completion 5,400 tokens -> estimate ~9.6k. Invoice shows 12.3k.

rachel_support: meter-bot attached recent invoice snapshot: https://billing.redwood.ai/invoices/INV-20260115-CA-123 (private link). Do you have any server logs or request-id from that run?

sasha_customer: The call-id from our logs is c-abc123. We also saw a server response header X-RWD-Request: rwd_20260115_abc123. No extra function calls on our side.

tim_eng: quick hypothesis: if the platform replaces base64 file contents with a server-side placeholder (eg. "<file:...>") or expands tool outputs into JSON fields after model tokenization, that could add tokens server-side that your estimator didn't account for. Can you share the raw SDK payload you passed before tokenization?

sasha_customer: The SDK sends the base64 blob inside the tools.input.contents field exactly as in the curl above; the estimator skips counting huge binary strings (we configured it to ignore known file fields to speed up local counting).

oliver_infra: digging into request rwd_20260115_abc123 — server did a post-processor that extracts the file, stores it, and replaces the tool input with metadata object: `{ "file_ref": "<file:abc123>", "sha256": "...", "size_bytes": 2345678 }`. That metadata is inserted into the message stream as a system-level message before the model call so the model can reference it. That insertion was not visible in the SDK/local estimator.

rachel_support: Ah — so server injected ~300 tokens of metadata JSON into the conversation before the model saw it. That matches the delta. Sasha, did your estimator include any server-side injected system messages?

sasha_customer: No — we intentionally ignore the file binary but not the server metadata since we didn't know it existed. Our estimator only counts the messages we send.

tim_eng: For a repro: run the same curl above but add `?trace=1` and we can show the exact tokenized input on the server side. Example: `curl 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions?trace=1' ...` — that returns a debug blob (admin-only) with the final messages sent to the model plus token counts. Can you run that and paste (redacted) output?

sasha_customer: Ran trace; attached snippet from trace response: 
```
final_messages: [
  {role: "system", content: "You are an assistant."},
  {role: "system", content: "file_meta: {\"file_ref\":\"<file:abc123>\",\"size_bytes\":2345678,\"sha256\":\"...\"}"},
  {role: "user", content: "Process this file and summarize."}
]
token_counts: prompt: 7200, completion: 5000
```

sasha_customer: That prompt 7,200 matches invoice math (7,200+5,100 ~= 12.3k). So server injection is the cause.

rachel_support: Good repro. Two actions: (1) short-term: we'll add a note in billing docs explaining server-side injected system/tool metadata can add tokens if you rely on local lightweight estimators; (2) medium-term: eng to add an opt-out that keeps raw tool input in client payload (so estimators see identical content) or returns pre-injection token delta in trace responses.

tim_eng: Implementation notes: the replacement and metadata insertion happen in the sidecar storager service. We can either (A) include metadata but not insert it as a model-visible system message (keep it off the message sequence, send separately to the tool hook), or (B) expose a header `X-RWD-Preserve-Tool-Inputs: true` that disables replacement — but that has storage/cost implications. I think adding a `trace` field that reports `server_injected_prompt_tokens: 300` is lowest friction for customers.

oliver_infra: I'll file infra task to surface `server_injected_prompt_tokens` in trace output and add a billing note about common injection sources (file metadata, request-level routing hints, language-detection preambles).

metering-bot: Recorded: case 2026-000874. Customer notified; ETA for trace field enhancement: ~2 weeks. :spiral_calendar:

sasha_customer: Thanks all — that explains it. For now we'll switch estimator to assume up to +500 tokens for file metadata until the trace field ships. Appreciate the quick triage. :thumbsup:
